newsitem.title: UK: UK government closes share payments NI loophole.
newsitem.headline: UK government closes share payments NI loophole.

text.p: The British government announced on Wednesday it was closing a loophole under which companies paying staff in their shares were able to avoid National Insurance contributions (NICs) on the benefit.
Pensions Minister Oliver Heald said the move, which will take effect from midnight (0000 GMT), would boost government revenues from National Insurance payments by 30 million stg a year.
The Social Security department said the new rules do not affect Inland Revenue-approved share schemes.
Heald said the crackdown was the latest in a series to prevent companies avoiding NICs by making payments in tradeable assets.
Schemes involving items such as coffee beans, gold bullion, fine wines and diamonds have already been ruled out of order by the government.

"We are committed to acting against exploitation of the National Insurance system by employers who undermine the contributory principle by avoiding paying their proper share of contributions on the earnings they pay to their employees," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
